## Questions and answers
### What can Cedar Lantern customers do with the billing export today, what are its current limits, and what is planned next?
supported: Cedar Lantern customers can use the billing export to generate a CSV report showing completed appointments and associated charges for a selected month\. The report includes the local appointment date, warehouse identifier, and charge amount\. Account administrators can download this CSV to reconcile monthly invoices, though it is not a tax document and does not modify or pay invoices\. The report is manually generated when the administrator requests it, so it may include corrections made after a prior download\. Administrators can download prior closed months as well as the current month, though the current month may be incomplete until the month ends\. The export is available to accounts on all paid plans, and only account administrators can generate it\. Support can explain column meanings but cannot generate exports from the support console\. The current billing export has several limits\. It is a manually downloaded CSV for one selected month, and only account administrators can generate it\. A month may contain corrections made after a prior download\. The export does not run on a schedule or send files by email, and it has no API\. It cannot export more than one account at a time, and there is no plan to provide a combined multi\-account report\. The file is in the currency used on the invoice for the account, with no conversion column, and comparisons between accounts in different currencies must happen outside the product\. The export does not support multiple accounts in the current screen\. The team plans to pilot scheduled email delivery with a small group in the third quarter of 2026\. An export API is only under consideration; it is not approved or scheduled\. The team has no commitment to provide a combined multi\-account report, and no decision was made to introduce cross\-account consolidation\. The roadmap is a statement of intent and remains subject to engineering review, security review, and competing priorities\. It is not evidence that a customer can use the feature today\.
